sources.title: Renormalizability of Massive Gravity in Three Dimensions

evidence.text: Can three-dimensional new massive gravity be shown perturbatively renormalizable while preserving the special higher-derivative structure underlying its previously claimed unitary massive spin-2 spectrum?

sources.title: Renormalization of Higher Derivative Quantum Gravity Coupled to a Scalar with Shift Symmetry

evidence.text: Does gravity coupled to a shift-symmetric scalar remain perturbatively renormalizable when both kinetic terms and interactions contain up to four derivatives, and how does the answer depend on D = 3, 4 or 5?

sources.title: FeynGrav 3.0

evidence.text: How can recursive geometric expansions improve FeynGrav’s generation of perturbative gravitational Feynman rules, and how can its supported models be extended to Horndeski, scalar–Gauss–Bonnet, axion-like, massive-spin-2, and quadratic-gravity sectors?

sources.title: Finiteness of quantum gravity coupled with matter in three space-time dimensions

evidence.text: Can three-dimensional quantum gravity coupled to interacting conformal matter be made finite by fixing irrelevant couplings, while retaining the Newton constant and matter marginal couplings as independent parameters?

sources.title: Renormalizability of Massive Gravity in Three Dimensions

evidence.text: Counts derivatives and internal lines in 1PI diagrams, improves ghost counting using the asserted graviton transversality, and combines the divergence bound with a linearized Slavnov-Taylor renormalization equation to classify local counterterms.

sources.title: Renormalization of Higher Derivative Quantum Gravity Coupled to a Scalar with Shift Symmetry

evidence.text: Spin-projector decomposition and inversion of the gauge-fixed quadratic action produce graviton and scalar propagators. In Landau gauge these are stated to fall as k⁻⁴, while the Faddeev-Popov ghost propagator falls as k⁻².

sources.title: FeynGrav 3.0

evidence.text: Introduce an auxiliary scaling h→zh and compare Jacobi’s determinant formula with the volume-factor series to derive a recurrence. Obtain recurrences for products of inverse metrics and the volume factor by multiplying series; extend the construction to vierbein factors.

sources.title: Finiteness of quantum gravity coupled with matter in three space-time dimensions

evidence.text: The two-loop calculation uses dimensional regularization with ε = 3−D and evaluates simple-pole residues in three dimensions. The paper acknowledges Chern–Simons tensor difficulties and relates poles to logarithms in an exponential-cutoff scheme.

sources.title: Renormalizability of Massive Gravity in Three Dimensions

evidence.text: Expands quadratic metric fluctuations in spin-2, spin-1, scalar, longitudinal, and mixed projection operators, then inverts the quadratic operator to analyze propagator components and poles.

sources.title: Renormalizability of Massive Gravity in Three Dimensions

evidence.text: BRST gauge fixing uses de Donder gauge for diffeomorphisms and a Landau-like condition for the Stückelberg vector. Sources for BRST variations are introduced to derive Slavnov-Taylor identities for the effective action.

sources.title: Positivity of Curvature-Squared Corrections in Gravity

evidence.text: What sign constraint does unitarity impose on the leading Gauss–Bonnet curvature-squared coefficient in pure gravity, when that operator is generated by a healthy tree-level ultraviolet completion?

sources.title: Quantum Gravity Constraints from Unitarity and Analyticity

evidence.text: Which quadratic and quartic curvature corrections to Einstein gravity are compatible with unitarity and analyticity of four-graviton scattering in a perturbative ultraviolet completion?

sources.title: Strict renormalizability as a paradigm for fundamental physics

evidence.text: Can strict perturbative renormalizability select a predictive gravitational QFT extending GR, with observational support already below the Planck scale?

sources.title: A Pedagogical explanation for the non-renormalizability of gravity

evidence.text: Why should gravity fail to admit a renormalizable local quantum-field-theory completion in the same spacetime dimension, using high-energy density of states rather than only perturbative irrelevance of Newton's coupling?

sources.title: Exorcising ghosts in quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can ghosts in finite higher-derivative gravity be interpreted as truncation artifacts and excluded through boundary conditions while retaining the ultraviolet behavior responsible for renormalizability?

sources.title: Perturbative unitarity of fractional field theories and gravity

evidence.text: Can fractional scalar, gauge and gravitational QFTs have perturbative unitarity compatible with ultraviolet renormalizability, and how do kinetic-operator definitions, Riemann-sheet choices and fakeon prescriptions affect their spectra and causality?

sources.title: Causality Constrains Higher Curvature Corrections to Gravity

evidence.text: Which signs of four-dimensional quartic Riemann corrections avoid positive ultraviolet graviton group-velocity shifts, and do quadratic or cubic curvature corrections modify propagation in the same approximation?

sources.title: Multidimensional finite quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can a nonpolynomial higher-derivative completion of Einstein gravity retain the physical graviton spectrum, make higher-loop amplitudes convergent in arbitrary dimension, and eliminate the remaining one-loop divergences through covariant Pauli–Villars conditions?

sources.title: Super-renormalizable or finite Lee–Wick quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can local gravity with finitely many higher derivatives combine Einstein behavior at low energy, perturbative super-renormalizability or finiteness, and Lee–Wick unitarity by allowing complex-conjugate poles while excluding additional real propagator poles?

sources.title: On the quantum field theory of the gravitational interactions

evidence.text: Can a local higher-derivative quantum field theory of gravity reconcile perturbative unitarity with renormalizability, and can a dimensionless gravitational gauge coupling select a unique model within this framework?

sources.title: Higher-derivative quantum gravity with purely virtual particles: renormalizability and unitarity

evidence.text: Can the massive spin-2 ghost required by renormalizable higher-derivative gravity be excluded from on-shell states while retaining its virtual contributions, thereby reconciling perturbative renormalizability and unitarity? The review also asks how this prescription affects inflationary observables.

sources.title: Self-Completeness of Einstein Gravity

evidence.text: Can pure Einstein gravity complete its own deep-UV physics through black-hole formation, without additional trans-Planckian propagating quantum fields or a Wilsonian UV fixed point?

sources.title: Ghost-free infinite derivative gravity

evidence.text: Can the four-derivative gravitational action containing R²/3 − RμνRμν receive a classically ghost-free completion through infinitely many higher derivatives, with a physical interpretation supplied by bimetric gravity?

sources.title: Renormalizable Quantum Gravity in Low Energy without Violating Unitarity

evidence.text: Can massive graviton ghost partners soften vacuum-energy and graviton-mass divergences at low energies while constraints on physical states preserve unitarity, and can this construction accommodate matter?

sources.title: Recent Progress in Fighting Ghosts in Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Under what conditions can higher-derivative quantum gravity reconcile renormalizability with unitarity and classical stability despite massive ghost states? The review emphasizes complex-pole Lee-Wick constructions and cosmological perturbation stability.

sources.title: Conformal Symmetry in Field Theory and in Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Can higher-derivative or weakly nonlocal gravity achieve UV finiteness, unitarity and non-anomalous local conformal symmetry, and what further constraints does conformality impose on effective actions and scattering?

sources.title: Renormalizable 4D Quantum Gravity as A Perturbed Theory from CFT

evidence.text: Can four-dimensional quantum gravity be organized as a renormalizable perturbation of a CFT with an exactly treated conformal mode, and how do anomalies and renormalization affect the cosmological constant and Planck mass?

sources.title: Unitarity versus Renormalizability of Higher Derivative Gravity in 3D

evidence.text: Can three-dimensional gravity with quadratic curvature terms be both perturbatively renormalizable and unitary around Minkowski space, especially at the new-massive-gravity coefficient choice? The paper also examines why an earlier renormalizability argument may fail.

sources.title: Super-renormalizable Higher-Derivative Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Can an infinite-derivative extension of quadratic gravity improve ultraviolet behavior while avoiding additional negative-residue propagator poles and rendering the point-source gravitational potential regular?

sources.title: Super-renormalizable Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Can an infinite-derivative extension of quadratic gravity retain only the physical graviton pole, become perturbatively super-renormalizable, reproduce Einstein gravity in the infrared, and soften classical black-hole singularities?

sources.title: Fakeons And Lee-Wick Models

evidence.text: Can theories containing physical particles and fakeons, including Lee-Wick higher-derivative theories, admit a consistent prescription that preserves perturbative unitarity to all orders and inherits Euclidean renormalization?

sources.title: Projectable Horava-Lifshitz gravity in a nutshell

evidence.text: The action is reduced using integration by parts with surface terms discarded, commutator and Bianchi identities, and the vanishing three-dimensional Weyl tensor. Excitations are studied by gauge-fixed perturbation theory about flat spacetime.

sources.title: Projectable Horava-Lifshitz gravity in a nutshell

evidence.text: Weighted engineering dimensions use [dx]=[κ]^-1 and [dt]=[κ]^-z. The leading gravitational kinetic and spatial couplings have dimension [κ]^(d−z); choosing z=d makes them dimensionless. A polynomial Lifshitz scalar provides the pedagogical comparison.

evidence.text: Can a self-contained quantum field theory of gravity in 3+1 dimensions improve ultraviolet behavior through anisotropic z=3 scaling, while relevant deformations produce relativistic scaling and potentially general relativity at long distances?

sources.title: Hořava gravity at a Lifshitz point: A progress report

evidence.text: Can anisotropic gravity improve ultraviolet behavior while avoiding ghosts and satisfying low-energy observations? This review assesses four versions, universal-horizon physics, nonrelativistic holography and progress toward quantization.

sources.title: Fakeons And Lee-Wick Models

evidence.text: Perform loop-energy integrals by residues, then deform spatial loop-momentum domains into complex values. Pinching regions are squeezed onto Lorentz-invariant surfaces; analytic extension to neighborhoods of those surfaces defines the final regions of analyticity.

sources.title: Ghost-free infinite derivative gravity

evidence.text: Solve δS/δf = 0 for f(g), then substitute into S[g,f]. The functional chain-rule contribution to δSeff/δg vanishes because f solves its own equation, giving the stated on-shell equivalence within the chosen solution class.

sources.title: Bound states of massive complex ghosts in superrenormalizable quantum gravity theories

evidence.text: For composite operators, compute a one-loop bubble and iterate it into a geometric Dyson-type series C=G_B/(1−λ₁₂G_B). Apply momentum subtraction, analytically continue the momentum, and search for real poles with positive residues.

sources.title: Triviality of higher derivative theories

evidence.text: Introduce an auxiliary field to obtain off-shell nilpotence and express the action as a total BRST transformation. Interactions are constructed through a prepotential U; eliminating the auxiliary field produces scalar interactions and corresponding ghost couplings.

sources.title: Fakeons And Lee-Wick Models

evidence.text: Define average continuation as half the sum of the two analytic continuations around a fakeon threshold. Apply it recursively at every such threshold, separating coincident thresholds through mass deformation before restoring the masses. Difference continuation is half the difference and organizes cut contributions.

sources.title: Fakeons And Lee-Wick Models

evidence.text: Use imported algebraic cutting equations, polynomial identities whose polarized-loop contributions vanish by contour integration. Derive generalized cutting equations at nonzero physical widths, continue them analytically within A0 and by averaging into other regions, then take the zero-width limit.

evidence.text: Can a local higher-derivative quantum field theory of gravity reconcile perturbative unitarity with renormalizability, and can a dimensionless gravitational gauge coupling select a unique model within this framework?

sources.title: dS Spaces and Brane Worlds in Exotic String Theories

evidence.text: Can residual ghosts be removed geometrically or suppressed sufficiently to leave reliable low-energy gauge scattering?

sources.title: Higher-derivative quantum gravity with purely virtual particles: renormalizability and unitarity

evidence.text: Can the massive spin-2 ghost required by renormalizable higher-derivative gravity be excluded from on-shell states while retaining its virtual contributions, thereby reconciling perturbative renormalizability and unitarity? The review also asks how this prescription affects inflationary observables.

sources.title: The Phantom menaced: Constraints on low-energy effective ghosts

evidence.text: How low must the ultraviolet cutoff of a scalar ghost effective theory be to suppress observable vacuum instability, and can a Lorentz-invariant cutoff suffice?

sources.title: Renormalizability of Massive Gravity in Three Dimensions

evidence.text: Can three-dimensional new massive gravity be shown perturbatively renormalizable while preserving the special higher-derivative structure underlying its previously claimed unitary massive spin-2 spectrum?

sources.title: Renormalizable Quantum Gravity in Low Energy without Violating Unitarity

evidence.text: Can massive graviton ghost partners soften vacuum-energy and graviton-mass divergences at low energies while constraints on physical states preserve unitarity, and can this construction accommodate matter?

sources.title: Recent Progress in Fighting Ghosts in Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Under what conditions can higher-derivative quantum gravity reconcile renormalizability with unitarity and classical stability despite massive ghost states? The review emphasizes complex-pole Lee-Wick constructions and cosmological perturbation stability.

sources.title: Reflection positivity in a higher-derivative model with physical bound states of ghosts

evidence.text: Does the composite bound-state operator in a previously proposed six-derivative scalar ghost model satisfy two-point Osterwalder–Schrader reflection positivity and admit a renormalized Källén–Lehmann representation with nonnegative spectral density?

sources.title: Unitary Issues in Some Higher Derivative Field Theories

evidence.text: Does eliminating ghost poles and improving ultraviolet behavior suffice for a higher-derivative theory to define a unitary fundamental quantum field theory? The paper tests this using Euclidean reflection positivity and spectral representations.
